messages:
sarah: FYI after the cni rollout (cilium v1.24, hybrid-mode enabled) west1 GPU nodepool is seeing increased east-west packet drops and queueing on inference pods. p95 latency spiked ~3x for inter-pod RPCs.
kevin: Noted. Which nodepool/ASG? Any correlation with MTU changes or kernel/kernel args? :thinking:
maria: west1-gpu-pool-3. We flipped hybrid-mode flag and bumped cilium to v1.24.0-rc2 earlier this morning via canary then full rollout. No kernel changes.
sarah: Short dumps: many pods show tx drops on the host veth/eni interfaces and cilium_host reports lots of 'fragmentation needed' in agent logs.
kevin: Can you paste a small log sample and an ip route/ip link output? Also run a quick iperf between two affected pods.
sarah: Logs and snippets below:

```
Mar 18 11:07:12 cilium-agent[1]: level=warn msg="fragmentation required" node=ip-10-2-3-45
Mar 18 11:07:13 kernel: veth0: tx_packets 123456 tx_errors 0 rx_packets 123000 rx_errors 6 dropped 3789
Mar 18 11:07:14 cilium-agent[1]: datapath: encapsulation mtu mismatch: local 9000 remote 1500 -> fragmenting
```

```
# ip -d link show ens6
4: ens6: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee ff brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff promisc on
    promiscuity 0 min_mtu 68 max_mtu 9000
```

```
# kubectl exec -it pod-a -- iperf3 -c pod-b -t 5
Connecting to host pod-b, port 5201
[ ID] Interval           Transfer     Bandwidth
[  4]   0.00-5.00   sec  620 MBytes   1.04 Gbits/sec  (lossy due to retransmits)
```

jordan: That iperf bandwidth isn't terrible, but retransmits + rx drops point to fragmentation or MTU mismatch caused by the recent change: hybrid-mode can enable both direct-routing and geneve paths which adjusts tunnel MTU. Our GPU nodes advertise jumbo frames (9000) and some transit links (CNIs/host routing) expect 1500, so encapsulation overhead is dropping effective path MTU to ~1450 in some flows.
kevin: Is RDMA involved? Any SR-IOV or RDMA HCA pinned to pods? That could make things worse if encapsulation forces fallback.
sarah: Most of the inference pods use SR-IOV passthrough on a subset of nodes. The failures are concentrated on pods on nodes that also host RDMA-enabled NICs. We see more drops where kernel shows offload mismatch (GSO/GRO offload flags toggled).
maria: Quick mitigation options:
- revert cilium to previous stable (v1.23.x) for west1 GPU nodepool only
- adjust cilium.tunnelMTU or disable hybrid geneve encapsulation for that nodepool
- force MTU tests and set host routes to consistent 9000 vs 1500

kevin: Rolling a targeted rollback seems least risky. Can we do a patch deploy command scoped to nodes with label gpu=true? Also need to cordon/drain scheduling safely.

jordan: Suggested command to patch daemonset image for kube-system cilium daemonset in west1 via nodeSelector override (example):

```
kubectl -n kube-system set image daemonset/cilium cilium=quay.io/cilium/cilium:v1.23.12
# then patch nodeSelector on the rollout or use node affinity in a kustomize overlay for the GPU pool
```

sarah: Also running a quick MTU probe across pods to confirm path MTU before rollback:

```
# from host
sudo ping -M do -s 8976 10.2.4.12
PING 10.2.4.12 (10.2.4.12) 8976(9004) bytes of data.
From 10.2.3.45 icmp_seq=1 Frag needed and DF set
```

kevin: That confirms fragmentation. Proceeding with a canary rollback on 3 nodes now. I'll cordon & drain then restart Cilium.

sarah: Noted, I'll hold the job scheduler for the affected ML jobs and re-route traffic using the console weight override for those zones.

deploy-bot: Rollout command received: rollback cilium -> v1.23.12 on nodes: ip-10-2-3-45, ip-10-2-3-46, ip-10-2-3-47. Start: 1777777789

oncall-infra: Heads-up — oncall paged for the GPU pool; keep logs and traces enabled (packetbeat + yggdrasil tracing).

kevin: Done patching 3 nodes. Pod restarts look clean. Re-running iperf and pings.

```
# after rollback
sudo ping -M do -s 8976 10.2.4.12
PING 10.2.4.12 (10.2.4.12) 8976(9004) bytes of data.
100% packet loss -> (but then after cilium v1.23, path negotiated at 9000 or handled properly)

# pod iperf
[ ID]   0.00-5.00 sec  1.45 GBytes  2.49 Gbits/sec  0.0% retransmits
```

maria: p95 latency back to baseline on canary nodes. Rolling the rest of west1-gpu-pool tomorrow with controlled window. We'll follow up with an engineer-facing postmortem that includes kernel offload flags and SR-IOV interactions.

jordan: Long-term: need automated MTU validation in our CNI upgrade playbook, and a preflight that checks for SR-IOV/RDMA NICs and host offload mismatches. Also evaluate patch to set cilium.tunnelMTU per nodepool.

sarah: Agree. Filing an ops ticket with checklist and remediation steps. Also suggest we add a small perf test to CI that runs iperf/ping MTU probes after any CNI change.

deploy-bot: Rollback finished: status=success time=1777777832

kevin: Great work team. Postmortem next steps: capture cilium-agent logs from the failing nodes, compile list of impacted jobs and cost impact (GPU idle time). Assigning to @maria for the write-up.

maria: On it. I'll include recommended config (disable hybrid-mode on GPU nodepools until we validate MTU) and the MTU probe commands. :white_check_mark:

sarah: Closing thread for now, reopen if recurrence. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
